messages.author: 20141cae1eb6d2fd
messages.subject: analysing a very small sample
parts:
Dear list,
I'm trying to estimate the density of a roe deer population in a small area (4900 ha), where it is assumed that the population is very small (a population crash was registered in 2003-2006). The area is almost all covered by Mediterranean maquis and forest.

We used line transect sampling and two observers covered 64 km of transects (the length of transects ranges from 0.4 to 1.6 km), 3 hours after sunrise and before sunset, using a lser range finder equipped with a compass to collect distance and angle data. The transects are located in a grid positioned randomly within the study area. The starting point is random within each grid cell. The orientation is random.

We carried out 4 replicates of the same set of transects (24 June - 25 September 2014; an average of 15 days to complete one survey) e we collected a total of 20 groups (3 in June-July, 3 in late July, 10 in August, 4 in September) and 22 roe deer. We surveyed in the same area also wild boars (tot groups collected: 939) and fallow deer (tot groups collected: 93).

To analyse data of the roe deer sampling, I used the MCDS analysis engine, I poststratified by replicate and I used a global detection function.
The longest perpendicular distance is 44.8 m. We miss observations in the interval 22-37 meters so I chose a truncation distance = g(x)=0.15 
(10m), discarding 3 observations.

I estimated a global density as a mean of replicates, weighted by total effort in each replicate, and I used a nonparametric bootstrap to estimate the variance of the density.
As expected, several error messages appeared:
**Warning: There are less than 10 data points per estimated parameter. Results may not be reliable.**
**Bootstrap Warning: There are no cluster size observations selected. Cannot estimate expected cluster size.**
**Bootstrap Warning: Number of cluster size measurements =  1  This is not sufficient to estimate a mean and variance**
**Bootstrap Warning: Estimation routine failed to converge as could not calculate area under pdf in iteration 48. Using results from previous iteration.**

Despite the very small sample, is this the right way to tackle with the analysis of this data in order to get a density estimate anyway?

Any suggestion to improve the analysis of so few observations? (without changing survey technique)

Cheers,
Barbara
